summary: Diff implements major frontend defenses against stale identity/cached data (principal-scoped React Query keys, comprehensive full logout cleanup, improved error messaging) and adjusts signup UI to remove client-side admin password checking. However, some backend-side pieces required to guarantee immediate post-signup permissions and caller-based enforcement are not fully evidenced in the provided backend diff (truncated), and several unrelated UI/product changes appear to be introduced.

missing_requirements.requirement: Ensure engineer signup immediately grants whatever access-control permission is required to call user endpoints right after signup (no Unauthorized/session-invalid loop).
missing_requirements.reason: Frontend calls `actor.processPendingSignups()` after `signupWithRole`, but the backend diff snippet does not show an implementation/export of `processPendingSignups` or the logic that assigns the caller a non-guest role immediately after signup. Because the backend file is truncated, this requirement cannot be confirmed as implemented from the provided evidence.

missing_requirements.requirement: Align admin signup password behavior between frontend and backend so admin signup can succeed when valid (as defined/checked by the backend), and incorrect passwords are rejected by the backend with a clear user-facing error.
missing_requirements.reason: Frontend-side removal of hardcoded validation is evidenced, but backend admin-signup password verification behavior and the admin-signup endpoint itself are not shown in the truncated `backend/main.mo` snippet (only `adminSignupPassword = "SecurePassword123"` is visible). Thus, end-to-end alignment/success criteria cannot be confirmed from the diff summary alone.

missing_requirements.requirement: Backend endpoints that return user-specific data enforce caller-based access correctly (non-admins cannot access other users’ profiles or reports).
missing_requirements.reason: While frontend adds principal-scoped caching to prevent UI leakage, the diff summary does not provide visible evidence of backend authorization checks on user-specific endpoints (e.g., `getUserProfile`, report listing/detail) beyond including authorization mixins. Due to truncation, it cannot be verified that all relevant endpoints enforce caller-based access correctly.
